result.summary: Implements BIP322 simple message signing and verification for native SegWit (P2WPKH, P2WSH) and Taproot (P2TR) addresses. Updates signmessage to generate BIP322 simple proofs using descriptor wallet signing machinery and updates verifymessage to verify witness stacks statelessly with the script interpreter. Preserves existing legacy P2PKH compact signatures while leaving P2SH (including nested SegWit), full signatures, and proofs of funds unsupported.
result.problem: The signmessage and verifymessage RPCs only support legacy compact signatures for P2PKH addresses. Users with funds in SegWit or Taproot addresses cannot prove ownership of an address or sign off-chain messages without executing on-chain transactions.
evidence: Addresses long-standing feature gap since the introduction of SegWit and Taproot, following up on closed PR #24058.

PR description: 'The message RPCs currently support legacy compact signatures for P2PKH addresses. This adds BIP322 simple proofs for native P2WPKH, P2WSH and P2TR addresses, allowing users to sign and verify messages for these addresses without creating an on-chain transaction.'
result.scope_notes: Includes upstream BIP322 test vectors (362 lines in src/test/data/bip322_vectors.json) under CC0-1.0; over 80% of the diff consists of unit, functional, and fuzz tests.
result.changed_since_previous: Refines the implementation to verify valid proofs in a single pass, isolates ephemeral MuSig2 nonces during one-shot signing so ongoing PSBT sessions are not disrupted, uses SIGHASH_DEFAULT for compact Taproot proofs, and adds targeted fuzzing for script-derived proofs.
result.card: Adds BIP322 simple message signing and verification for native P2WPKH, P2WSH, and P2TR addresses to signmessage and verifymessage. Currently, message signing RPCs only support legacy P2PKH addresses, preventing SegWit and Taproot users from proving address control without spending on-chain. Verification is stateless and executed via Core's script interpreter, while signing utilizes wallet descriptor machinery (including Miniscript and Taproot key/script paths). Legacy P2PKH behavior is preserved, while P2SH, full proofs, and proofs of funds remain unsupported.

risk.why: Bugs in virtual transaction construction or wallet signing could corrupt message proof generation or mishandle signing nonces, and verification bugs could falsely authenticate invalid signatures.
